about: The Brackens' heather moor: a low ridge of peat and gritstone with ling, bilberry, bracken and gorse, sheep-bitten turf on the ways between, Scots pines on the crest. A brief as data (rules-system.md 4, 'Adding a biome'), from draft #182's moor_kit, which is frozen; the kit owner ports its techniques. Every family is a house ramp (art/house-palette.json). Numbers are shares of walkable ground unless named otherwise. 'kit' is pinned when kit v1 (woodland@1) exists.
palette_intent: Purple-brown and olive, warmer and drier than the valley's meadow: heather reads as one dusky purple-brown from afar and as many small lit tufts up close; the turf yellows towards the gap and the steppe beyond; peat faces are dark cool brown with red-brown sphagnum; grit is pale grey. Flowers are rare and clustered (mauve ling tips, gorse yellow), never speckle.

ground.base: turf: grass with warm and cool siblings in broad patches (scale about 7 texels at 1x), dry sand_warm patches growing towards the gap (yellow 0.25 inside the ridge, 0.5 at the gap)

drifts.name: heather
drifts.recipe: clumped tufts 1.9 to 2.8 texels across on an earth base; half mauve (dusk_warm) and half brown (earth_warm), more mauve where the drift flowers; each tuft lit on its top left, a tone apart at most; berry_cool tips on a few lit crowns

drifts.name: bracken
drifts.recipe: fronds in drifts on the deeper ground below the heather: grass_warm and leaf_warm, three-texel diagonal stamps, a few clay dead fronds

drifts.name: grit
drifts.recipe: pale stone where the peat is thin, with sparse pebbles

inside_heather.bilberry: a quarter of the tufts in shadier drifts turn leaf green

ground.calm: despeckle after every pass; texture swaps at most 14 % within a drift and ups and downs of 2 to 3 %; no lone pixels (SB-05)

plants.where: everywhere on the ridge and bluff tops, thinning at the foot of faces
deeper soil: the valley side, foot of the bluffs, hollows
clumps along the trods and on the west side, thickening into thicket at the edge
plants.sizes: three, 28 x 20 texels the largest at 1x
plants.flowers: clustered brass tips on the lit side only

plants.where: singly and in twos on the crest and the north bluff; never in a row
only in the wet flushes below springs and the drove well
in small drifts on the sheep's ways, yellow in pairs of texels

clusters.where: beside a trod at a bend, the trod's side away from the drop
crest and north bluff tops, on a rim cell, never on a path
ridge rims, the stone ring's ridge, the gap's bluffs
beside the sheepfolds along the Drover's Road
below the drove well and springs, down the slope

tiers.notes: two or three tiers (the brief): 32 px peat-and-grit faces on the bluffs, 16 px turf banks on the ridge's terraces; rims kept a face plus a cell apart (no 64 px stacked faces)

edges.from_woodland: The face is peat over gritstone, not the woodland's earth bank: dark cool peat in hags with red-brown sphagnum in the upper third, grey gritstone courses showing at the foot of the taller bluffs. The lip is heather overhanging by one or two texels with a few hanging tufts, not a sod roll. The foot is grit and fallen peat crumbs, with bracken grown into it. Side bands step in by whole cells (to-all-grid-2x). Volume (to-all-volume): bluffs step in and out by whole cells as hags and buttresses, lit top-left planes, a cast shadow at the foot.
edges.stair: rough gritstone steps between heather cheeks; timber only at the sheepfolds
edges.bank: peat bank with cotton grass and rush on the drove well's flush; no reeds

water.notes: the moor holds little open water: the drove well's trough and its flush, two springs on the north bluff's foot; no streams cross the ridge

ambience.light: the moor sits west of the valley: late light reaches it last, so dusk warms the heather

transitions.where: the valley side of the Brackens
transitions.how: heath blend: heather drifts break into tufts, then into turf with tormentil (river_kit.heath's idea)
turf yellowing to sand_warm, then D's steppe band; gorse thins out

transitions.where: the north 544 px, the massif's front
transitions.how: grit share rising to scree and boulders under the first crag faces
